newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end sharply lower on falling pork prices.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end sharply lower on falling pork prices.

text.p: CME hog futures finished mostly lower to sharply lower on selling sparked by sliding cash pork prices and weaker cash hog values, traders said. Spillover weakness again weighed on pork bellies at the close.

Hogs closed 1.175 cent a lb lower to 0.075 higher with only October up and December off most at 57.625 cent. February ended 0.900 lower at 74.950 cents, 1-1/2 month low. Pork bellies finished 1.075 cent a lb lower to 0.200 higher with February off most at 77.250 cents.
Commercial and fund liquidation touched off sell stops in hogs on the setback with only some light support cited.
"The product (price break) is leading to the downfall of hogs," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.

Most cash pork products were lower again at noon and cutout values have already fallen $4.50 per cwt since the first of the month. This prompted ideas of lower cash hog markets again Thursday, possibly down another $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt, traders said.
Rand Financials, Rosenthal Collins, R.J. O'Brien and Lind-Waldock notably sold, pit sources said.
In hog options, there was general buying of February 74 to 80 calls and selling of April 76 calls, pit sources added.
Although fundamentals were stronger in pork belly futures, spillover pressure from hog futures kept prices down. General selling followed the break in hogs, traders said.

Support at times reflected further strength in cash bellies, the recent light pace of slaughter and low stored stocks. Cash bellies were the only primary product showing strength the past couple of days and were quoted steady to up $1 at noon, sources noted.

Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town report was also mildly bullish to futures. The data showed a net in-movement of 1.779 million lbs of bellies into CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago. The total was within the range of analysts' estimates of in 1.5 million to 2.5 million lbs. The movement into storage left total stocks below year-ago levels.
Refco and Lind-Waldock sold late. Rand Financials and Paine Webber were early buyers, pit sources added.
